OIML-CS certificates of conformity can be issued under scheme A or B. This is a 2006 PTB certificate, before OIML-CS existed (OIML-CS started 2004 actually). R60/2000-DE1-06.01 format is a classic national certificate. I'll set scheme "A" since it's a certificate of conformity issued by an issuing authority... Actually classic OIML certificates are not OIML-CS. But the schema requires scheme (A|B). I'll put "A" as it's the closest (single issuing authority evaluation). Hmm, risky fabrication. The certificate doesn't state a scheme. Rule 8: don't fabricate. But the schema lists scheme as required in certificate. I could omit it since not present. Safer to omit? The schema shows `number, scheme (A|B), ...` — these seem expected. The "R60/2000-DE1-06.01" suggests classic OIML certificate format. OIML scheme A is "certificate issued on the basis of... " I'll omit scheme since not explicitly in document. Actually, hmm. Many extractors would set "A". Let me omit it to follow rule 8.

Actually wait — the layered schema lists fields; rule 8 says if a field is not present in the markdown, omit it. Scheme is not present. Omit.

- project_number: R3-0033? That's a PTB document reference number "R3-0033". Hmm, could be PTB's internal registration. It's listed at bottom of page 1. It might be the PTB project/registration number. I'll include it as project_number: "R3-0033". Risky? It appears to be a reference number of PTB. I think including it as project_number is reasonable.
